## Context

Make `rebar bridge preview` and `rebar bridge sync` the primary vocabulary without breaking
existing CLI, direct-engine, Python-library, MCP, workflow, or helper callers. This is an
expand-contract migration: legacy entrypoints remain explicit adapters because their defaults
and filtering semantics differ from the canonical surface.

## Decisions and scope

- `rebar reconcile` and `rebar.reconcile()` remain dry-run by default; argument-less
  `python -m rebar_reconciler` and `bridge sync` remain live.
- Legacy `--mode` and `--filter-local-ids` remain supported. Canonical `--only`/`--except`
  filter before differs; the legacy flag continues filtering writes after full examination.
- `Mode`, `MODE_CAPS`, and `gated_mode: reconcile-check` remain for old readers, phase-gate
  safety, and checked-out workflow revisions.
- The production workflow uses canonical vocabulary except `reconcile-check`, which remains the
  lock-free diagnostic `rebar reconcile --mode reconcile-check`; only dry-run maps to preview.
- `--max-changes` is an explicit canonical live cap. It reuses the shared partition seam and
  retains a deterministic audit manifest even when the ceiling is not reached. Uncapped live and
  legacy bootstrap behavior remain unchanged.
- The normalized request is built before lock acquisition. Selection syntax/resolution is
  read-only and pre-lock; the selected IDs are revalidated against the locked load before any
  differ or mutation.
- The shared core stays Python-first. Parser/normalization lives in `request.py`; selection uses
  the existing helper seam; provider/workflow files remain declarative callers.
- Library and MCP bridge additions belong to sibling `f789`; this ticket keeps legacy
  `reconcile` facades callable and proves their continuity.
- `--max-age` belongs to bridge status story `b69c`, not preview/sync.
- ADR 0092, its collision-proof reservation, and the generated ADR index record why explicit
  compatibility adapters are required. The number/index follow the repository's current ADR
  convention.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] Canonical CLI preview/sync route through primary engine subcommands.
- [x] Argument-less `rebar reconcile` remains dry-run and every legacy `--mode` retains its
      documented behavior and numeric result.
- [x] Direct engine `--mode` calls and argument-less live default remain functional while
      canonical requests normalize into the same core execution path.
- [x] Legacy `--filter-local-ids` retains post-differ write filtering; canonical `--only` and
      `--except` narrow all differ inputs before differs run.
- [x] `Mode`, `MODE_CAPS`, and the `reconcile-check` phase-gate value remain available to old
      readers and workflows.
- [x] Public Python `rebar.reconcile(...)` and MCP `reconcile(mode=...)` remain callable with
      historical defaults and gating behavior.
- [x] The production workflow uses canonical vocabulary for mapped operations while retaining
      the exact `reconcile-check` diagnostic path and rollback compatibility.
- [x] Pressure-test scripts, Jira helpers, current docs, and generated references use canonical
      vocabulary; explicit compatibility fixtures retain legacy spellings.
- [x] Real-entrypoint tests cover mapped success, failure, gate, pause, in-flight, output, cap,
      and exit behavior without collapsing distinct no-argument defaults.
- [x] Primary help avoids internal vocabulary; compatibility help and release notes state every
      old-to-new mapping and retained default.
- [x] `bridge sync --max-changes 10` and `100` apply deterministic 10/100 partitions; invalid,
      zero, and negative caps exit 2 before lock or mutation.
- [x] Explicit capped live runs retain deterministic applied/deferred manifests for 10/92,
      100/2, and 102/0; uncapped live still removes its temporary manifest.
- [x] Every `--only`/`--except` token must resolve to an existing local ID or bound Jira key;
      empty, partial, or wholly unresolved input exits 2 before lock, sync, fetch, or mutation.
- [x] A target that disappears between preflight and the locked load exits 2, names the missing
      IDs, releases the lock, and calls no differ, applier, manifest, or persistence seam.
- [x] The legacy external-DC helper and its compatibility consumers retain `--mode` plus
      `--filter-local-ids`; additive primary helpers do not silently rewrite those fixtures.
- [x] ADR 0092, its reservation marker, generated index, architecture link, and release link pass
      the current ADR numbering/index checks and record the adapter/capped-manifest rationale.
- [x] Legacy CLI, direct-engine, library, MCP, workflow, and external-helper entrypoints remain
      shippable for environments still using the old vocabulary.

## Verification evidence

- Real surfaces: `tests/interfaces/facades/test_bridge_cli_heldout.py`,
  `tests/interfaces/facades/test_cli.py`, `tests/interfaces/facades/test_library.py`, and
  `tests/interfaces/facades/test_mcp.py`.
- Engine contracts: `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/orchestrate/test_reconcile_main.py`,
  `test_reconcile_filter.py`, and `test_mode_cap_enforcement.py`.
- Workflow/docs generation: `tests/unit/workflow/test_reconcile_workflow_lint.py` and
  `tests/unit/test_gen_cli_reference.py`.
- Merged implementation: Gerrit change 1595 ancestry through
  `694cf894def36241724e7049e3308d782037ef6d`, with LLM-Review +1 and Verified +1.

## Residual disposition

Canonical and legacy CLI/engine/library/MCP directions, automated callers, workflows, current
docs, capped sync, selection races, and old-vocabulary continuity are fixed in scope and covered.
Bridge-shaped library/MCP operations are completed by sibling `f789`; bridge status `--max-age`
is completed by sibling `b69c`. No compatibility surface is intentionally removed here.
